scenes.say: That sudden puff of air during an eye test. Do you know what it actually checks?

scenes.en: It measures the pressure inside your eye. Painless, takes seconds.
scenes.say: It measures the pressure inside your eye. It's painless, quick, and nothing touches your eye.

scenes.en: If eye fluid drains too slowly, pressure can harm the optic nerve.
scenes.say: Your eye keeps making and draining a clear fluid. If it drains too slowly, pressure can build up and damage the optic nerve. This is linked to glaucoma.

scenes.en: Glaucoma often has no pain and no early signs. Lost vision can't come back.
scenes.say: Did you know? Glaucoma often has no pain and no early warning signs. Side vision is lost slowly, and lost vision cannot be brought back.

scenes.en: Over 40, family history, diabetes, high short sight
scenes.say: Your risk is higher if you're over forty, if a parent or sibling has glaucoma, if you have diabetes, or if you have high short sight.

scenes.en: Sudden eye pain, red eye, headache, halos around lights
scenes.ta: திடீர் கண் வலி, சிவப்பு, ஒளியைச் சுற்றி வளையம்: உடனே மருத்துவரிடம்
scenes.say: See an eye specialist urgently if you get sudden severe eye pain, a red eye, a headache with vomiting, or rainbow halos around lights.
The puff test is one part of glaucoma screening, along with checking the optic nerve. Over forty? Get checked every year. Book an eye test today.
